optionCases.b: Wrong: the recommendation comes last, not first.
optionCases.c: Wrong: only a passing reference to the previous year appears, and comparability is said to be limited.
optionCases.d: Correct: paragraph 1 gives figures, paragraph 2 the methodological limits, paragraph 3 a recommendation 'sous ces réserves'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'le faire' replaces the action verb 'répondre', not being dissatisfied (which is the subject's attribute).
optionCases.b: Correct: 'le faire' takes up 'répondre', i.e. responding to the survey questionnaire.
optionCases.c: Wrong: reaching an agent belongs to a different sentence and is unrelated to response bias.
optionCases.d: Wrong: interpreting with caution is what the analysts do, not what the clients might be inclined to do.

optionCases.a: Wrong: the benefit was paid retroactively, not refused.
optionCases.b: Wrong: the missing document is history; the file is closed and the benefit paid.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the letter concedes the delay complaint and apologizes.
optionCases.d: Correct: it addresses each grievance in turn, admits the department's omission and informs her of the review recourse.

optionCases.a: Wrong: the department could not trace the exchanges and admits nothing; the conditional 'auriez reçue' keeps the claim at a distance.
optionCases.b: Wrong: no blame is placed on the client's understanding.
optionCases.c: Correct: unable to trace the exchanges, the department neither confirms nor denies, while reminding staff of the rules as a precaution.
optionCases.d: Wrong: only a reminder of current instructions is mentioned, not disciplinary action.

optionCases.a: Correct: she names the specific omission (the document should have been requested at once) and apologizes outright.
optionCases.b: Wrong: she states the omission is in no way the client's responsibility.
optionCases.c: Wrong: she gives a clear cause for the delay.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the letter uses formal correspondence conventions throughout.

optionCases.a: Wrong: the body is organized by grievance, not by the file's chronology.
optionCases.b: Correct: delay first, contradictory information second (the order of the opening summary), then the payment status and the review recourse.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the delay is addressed before the contradictory information.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the payment is mentioned near the end, not first, and there is no decision followed by reasons.

optionCases.a: Wrong: it reverses the meaning; the phrase exonerates the client.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'responsabilité' here is fault, not jurisdiction, and the office does handle the complaint.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'ne relève en rien de votre responsabilité' means the client cannot be held at fault in any way.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the letter says the omission contributed to the delay.

registerFlag.note: Stem uses 'qualifie l'oubli du Ministère comme ne relevant…'; standard French is 'qualifier de', and 'qualifier … comme' is a construction usage guides reject. Should read e.g. 'présente l'oubli … comme ne relevant…'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: the preceding direct object 'que' (= les dossiers, masc. pl.) requires agreement.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'dossiers' is masculine.
optionCases.c: Correct: the participle with avoir agrees with the preceding COD 'que' = 'les dossiers' (masc. pl.).
optionCases.d: Wrong: agrees with the subject 'elle', which avoir does not allow.

optionCases.a: Correct: the participle of impersonal 'falloir' is always invariable.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'que' is not a direct object of impersonal 'il a fallu'; no agreement.
optionCases.c: Wrong: no agreement and wrong number/gender.
optionCases.d: Wrong: no agreement with 'somme' for an impersonal verb.

optionCases.a: Wrong under the standard rule: with the partitive pronoun 'en' as preceding COD, the participle stays invariable; agreement with 'demandes' is an occasional literary variant, not the accepted norm.
optionCases.b: Wrong: masculine plural matches nothing in the sentence.
optionCases.c: Wrong: feminine singular matches nothing and ignores the 'en' rule.
optionCases.d: Correct: a participle preceded by 'en' as COD generally remains invariable.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'se' is an indirect object (succéder à), so no agreement.
optionCases.b: Correct: 'se sont succédé' is invariable because 'se' is the indirect object.
optionCases.c: Wrong: no agreement possible, and 'gestionnaires' is not specified as feminine.
optionCases.d: Wrong: feminine singular agreement with nothing.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'quel que' + être agrees with the subject 'les contraintes' (fem. pl.): 'Quelles que soient'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'quelque' in one word precedes an adjective or noun, not the verb être.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'contraintes' is feminine.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'quelques' (several) makes no sense before a verb.

optionCases.a: Wrong: after the noun, 'demi' agrees in gender with it ('heure' is feminine).
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'demi' after the noun agrees in gender only, never in number.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'deux heures et demie': gender agreement with 'heure', singular.
optionCases.d: Wrong: wrong gender and number.

optionCases.a: Wrong: placed after the noun, 'nu' agrees with 'pieds' (masc. pl.).
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'pieds' is masculine.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'pieds' is masculine plural.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'pieds nus': the adjective follows the noun and agrees with it.

optionCases.a: Wrong: adverbial 'tout' agrees before a feminine adjective beginning with a consonant.
optionCases.b: Correct: 'toute fière': 'tout' takes the feminine form before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the subject is singular.
optionCases.d: Wrong: masculine plural does not fit a singular feminine subject.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'cent' takes no 's' when followed by another numeral such as 'mille'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'mille' is invariable and 'cent' followed by mille takes no 's'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'mille' (the numeral) is invariable.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'deux cent mille': cent followed by another number and mille invariable.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'plus d'un' + singular noun normally takes a singular verb; the participle with avoir and a following COD is invariable.
optionCases.b: Wrong: plural after 'plus d'un' is reserved for reciprocal meaning or a repeated 'plus d'un', neither of which applies.
optionCases.c: Wrong: plural verb and an incorrect participle agreement with a following COD.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the participle cannot agree with a COD that follows it.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'soumissions' is feminine.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'l'une ou l'autre' means only one of them, which contradicts both meeting the requirements, and fits poorly with plural 'seront'.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'l'une et l'autre' (fem.) refers to both bids and takes the plural verb 'seront soumises'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'chacune' requires a singular verb ('sera soumise').

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'que' (= les trois heures) is an adverbial complement of duration, not a direct object, so no agreement.
optionCases.b: Correct: with 'durer', the duration is a circumstantial complement and the participle stays invariable.
optionCases.c: Wrong: agreement with the subject 'panne' is not possible with avoir.
optionCases.d: Wrong: no agreement, and masculine plural matches nothing.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'laissé' + infinitive is invariable under the 1990 rectifications, and also under the traditional rule here since she undergoes rather than performs the convincing.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'laisser' takes a bare infinitive, not a participle, and the agreement is also wrong.
optionCases.c: Correct: 's'est laissé convaincre': laissé followed by an infinitive stays invariable.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'laisser' must be followed by an infinitive, not a participle.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'la plupart des' + plural noun takes a plural verb.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'assister à' is intransitive, so the participle is invariable.
optionCases.c: Wrong: singular verb plus a wrong participle agreement.
optionCases.d: Correct: plural verb after 'la plupart des employés', invariable participle.

optionCases.a: Correct: when 'le peu de' expresses insufficiency (the lack is what harmed), the verb agrees with 'le peu' in the singular; 'nui' is invariable.
optionCases.b: Wrong here: plural agreement fits when 'le peu' means a small but existing quantity, whereas the context stresses that the shortage itself did the harm.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'nuire' is intransitive, so 'nui' never agrees.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'nui' is invariable.

optionCases.a: Wrong: in a general procedure 'on' is indefinite, so the attribute stays masculine singular; plural agreement fits only when 'on' clearly stands for a specific group (= nous).
optionCases.b: Correct: indefinite 'on' takes a singular verb and a masculine singular attribute.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'on' always takes a third-person singular verb.
optionCases.d: Wrong: plural verb with 'on' is ungrammatical.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'fait' followed by an infinitive is always invariable.
optionCases.b: Correct: invariable 'fait' + infinitive, and the plural subject 'vérifications' takes 'ont confirmé'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the main verb must agree with the plural subject 'les vérifications'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'fait' + infinitive never agrees.

optionCases.a: Wrong: a polite 'vous' addressed to one person takes a singular attribute.
optionCases.b: Wrong: the person addressed is a woman ('Madame la Présidente').
optionCases.c: Wrong: singular and feminine are required.
optionCases.d: Correct: polite 'vous' for one woman, so feminine singular 'invitée'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'quelque' before an adjective is an adverb and invariable.
optionCases.b: Wrong: the subject 'les réviseurs' requires plural 'doivent'.
optionCases.c: Correct: invariable adverb 'quelque' + adjective + que + subjunctive, and plural 'doivent'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'quel que' is used only directly before être, not before an adjective.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'eux-mêmes' is plural like 'eux', and the participle with avoir and a following COD is invariable.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'même' agrees in number with the plural pronoun.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the COD follows the participle, so 'suivi' is invariable.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'directeurs généraux' is masculine.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'se' is an indirect object (permettre à soi), so no agreement.
optionCases.b: Wrong: no agreement, and the number is wrong too.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the subject is plural.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'se sont permis de': 'se' is an indirect object, so the participle is invariable.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'approuvées' is a passive participle agreeing with 'factures', correctly.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'plusieurs factures' is plural, so 'avaient' is correct.
optionCases.c: Correct: in 'se rendre compte', 'compte' is the COD and 'se' indirect, so 'rendu' is invariable.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the present participle 'détenant' is invariable.

optionCases.a: Correct: subjects of different persons joined by 'ni… ni' take the plural, and the first person wins: 'ni elle ni moi ne pourrons'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: third-person singular ignores the first-person 'moi'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'nous vous transmettrons' is already correct.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'commentaires' is masculine, so 'écrits' is correct.

optionCases.a: Wrong: a simple colour adjective agrees, so 'jaunes' is correct.
optionCases.b: Correct: compound colour adjectives ('bleu foncé') are invariable.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'livrables' is masculine.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'en attente' is an invariable prepositional phrase.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'cents' keeps its 's' when multiplied and not followed by another numeral.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'organisée' correctly agrees with 'journée'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'participer' takes no direct object, so 'participé' is invariable.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'quelque' meaning 'about' before a numeral is an invariable adverb.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'quatre-vingts' takes an 's' when multiplied and not followed by another numeral.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'vingt et une' agrees with the feminine 'demandes'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'demandes' is feminine, so 'acceptées' is correct.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the COD follows the participle, so 'présenté' is invariable.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'leurs identifiants' correctly agrees with the plural possessor and plural noun.
optionCases.b: Wrong: with avoir and no preceding direct object, 'reçu' stays invariable.
optionCases.c: Right: the indirect object pronoun 'leur' never takes an s.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'puissent' correctly agrees with the plural subject 'ils'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'destinés' correctly agrees with 'messages' (masculine plural).
optionCases.b: Wrong: after 'afin de' the infinitive 'harmoniser' is required.
optionCases.c: Right: in 'se parler' the pronoun is an indirect object (parler à), so the participle stays invariable: 'se sont parlé'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'régionaux' correctly agrees with 'médias' (masculine plural).

optionCases.a: Wrong: the subject 'conseillères' is feminine, so the masculine plural is still incorrect.
optionCases.b: Right: 's'absenter' is essentially pronominal, so the participle agrees with the feminine plural subject: 'absentées'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'offert' correctly agrees with 'l'atelier' (masculine singular).
optionCases.d: Wrong: after 'pour' the infinitive 'assister' is required.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'se consacrer' has 'se' as direct object, so 'consacrée' correctly agrees with 'l'équipe'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'survenu' correctly agrees with 'l'incident' (masculine).
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'diffusées' correctly agrees with 'consignes' (feminine plural).
optionCases.d: Right: adverbial 'tout' (meaning 'entirely') stays invariable before a feminine adjective beginning with a vowel: 'tout entière'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'questions' is feminine, so 'toutes' is correct.
optionCases.b: Right: after 'c'est moi qui', the verb agrees with 'moi' in the first person: 'qui ai préparé'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the subject is 'vous', so 'pouvez' is correct.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'concernant' is used as an invariable preposition here.

optionCases.a: Right: placed after the noun it qualifies, 'ci-joint' agrees: 'les deux formulaires ci-joints'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: with avoir and the direct object 'votre demande' placed after, 'reçu' stays invariable.
optionCases.c: Wrong: after 'veuillez ... et nous les', an infinitive 'retourner' is required, not a participle.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'les' (the forms) is the direct object of 'retourner'; 'leur' would be an incorrect indirect object.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'se déclarer' has 'se' as direct object, so 'déclarée' correctly agrees with 'la sous-ministre'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'accomplis' correctly agrees with 'progrès' (masculine plural).
optionCases.c: Right: the attribute adjective must agree with 'la sous-ministre': 'satisfaite'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'présenté' correctly agrees with 'le prochain bilan' (masculine).

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'se rappeler' takes a direct object in careful usage; 'se rappeler de quelque chose' is criticized.
optionCases.b: Right: 'se souvenir de quelque chose' is the correct construction.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'se souvenir' requires the preposition 'de' before its complement.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'se souvenir à' is not a French construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong in the target register: 'être en charge de' is a calque of 'in charge of' that GC style guides advise against.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'responsable pour' is an anglicism; the construction is 'responsable de'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'chargé' governs 'de', not 'à', for a responsibility.
optionCases.d: Right: 'être chargée de' is the standard construction for an assigned responsibility.

optionCases.a: Right: 'suite à' is a criticized usage in careful administrative writing; GC guides prescribe 'à la suite de'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'avant ou le' is a calque of 'on or before' and is itself an error.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'révisées' correctly agrees with 'descriptions' (feminine plural).
optionCases.d: Wrong: the adverb is 'conformément à', not 'conformément avec'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'consister à' introduces an infinitive, not a noun phrase.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'consister de' is an anglicism (consist of).
optionCases.c: Right: 'consister en' introduces a noun phrase ('une réduction progressive').
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'consister sur' is not a French construction.

optionCases.a: Right: 'au chapitre de' is the idiomatic administrative expression for 'with respect to'.
optionCases.b: Wrong in register: figurative 'au niveau de' meaning 'regarding' is criticized by GC style guides.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the locution is 'au chapitre de', not 'au chapitre à'.
optionCases.d: Wrong in register: 'en termes de' meaning 'in terms of' is a criticized anglicism.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'qui s'est tenue' correctly agrees with 'la séance'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'séance d'information sur' is the correct construction.
optionCases.c: Right: 'assister' in the sense of attending requires 'à': 'ont assisté à la séance'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'mardi dernier' takes no preposition.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'participer dans' is an anglicism.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'participer' requires 'à' before its complement.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'participer de' means 'to partake of the nature of', not to attend.
optionCases.d: Right: 'participer à la séance' is the correct construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'dans deux semaines' refers to a point in the future, which contradicts the past action.
optionCases.b: Right: 'en deux semaines' expresses the time taken to complete the action.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'depuis deux semaines' implies an ongoing action, inconsistent with the completed migration.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'pour deux semaines' expresses an intended duration and is not idiomatic here.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'éviter que' requires the subjunctive 'se reproduise'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'la dernière année' is a calque; 'l'an dernier' is correct.
optionCases.c: Right: 'se rappeler' takes a direct object: 'Je me rappelle la panne'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the correct form is 'à l'automne', not 'en l'automne'.

optionCases.a: Right: 's'attendre à ce que' plus the subjunctive is the correct construction.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 's'attendre de ce que' is not standard.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'à que' is ungrammatical; 'à ce que' is required.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'attendre' without the pronoun has a different meaning, and 'attend à ce que' is ungrammatical.

optionCases.a: Wrong: masculine provinces starting with a consonant take 'au', not 'en'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: cities take 'à', not 'en'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: provinces take 'au' or 'en', not 'à'.
optionCases.d: Right: 'à Moncton' (city) and 'au Nouveau-Brunswick' (masculine province) are both correct.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'en Ontario' is correct (vowel-initial province).
optionCases.b: Right: cities take 'à': 'à Ottawa'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: after 'faire' the infinitive is required.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'en ligne' is the correct expression.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'consister en' introduces a noun phrase, not an infinitive.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'consister de' is an anglicism.
optionCases.c: Right: 'consister à' introduces the infinitive 'formuler'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'consister pour' is not a French construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'sous l'article' is a calque of 'under section'; legal French uses 'en vertu de'.
optionCases.b: Right: 'en vertu de l'article 7' is the standard legal and administrative construction.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the locution is 'en vertu de', not 'en vertu à'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'en fonction de' means 'depending on' and does not express legal authority.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'obvier sur' is not a French construction.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'assorti de' is correct; 'assorti avec' is not the right construction here.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'hebdomadaire' correctly agrees with 'suivi' (singular).
optionCases.d: Right: 'obvier' is transitive indirect: 'obvier aux retards'.

optionCases.a: Right: 'faire face à' plus a complement is the correct construction.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'faire face' requires 'à' before its complement.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'faire face avec' is not a French construction.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'faire face contre' is not a French construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'se conformer avec' is incorrect; the verb governs 'à'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: the verb is pronominal in this sense ('se conformer').
optionCases.c: Right: 'se conformer aux consignes' is the correct construction.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'se conformer de' is not a French construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'en consigne les résultats' (the results of the inspection) is correct; 'y' would be the wrong pronoun.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'l'inspection des lieux' is correct.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'consigner dans un registre' is correct.
optionCases.d: Right: 'responsable pour' is an anglicism; the correct form is 'responsable de'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'satisfaire avec' is not a French construction.
optionCases.b: Right: 'satisfaire à des exigences' is the standard construction in procurement French.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'satisfaire de' is not the construction for meeting requirements.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'répondre' requires 'à' ('ne répond pas à'), so the bare form is ungrammatical.

optionCases.a: Right: 'conformément aux critères' is the precise standard construction.
optionCases.b: Wrong in nuance and register: 'en lien avec' only means 'related to' and does not express compliance with the criteria.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the adverb is 'conformément à', not 'conformément avec'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: the locution is 'dans le respect des', not 'dans le respect avec'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'relatif à' is the correct construction.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'sur réception de' is the fixed expression; adding the article is not the error being tested and is less idiomatic.
optionCases.c: Right: 'à compter de' requires 'de': 'à compter du 1er avril'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 's'appliquer à' is the correct construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong in register: 'suite à' is criticized in careful administrative writing.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'dû à' used as a prepositional locution is a criticized anglicism, and it gives a causal rather than temporal meaning.
optionCases.c: Wrong: the locution is 'à la suite de', not 'à la suite à'.
optionCases.d: Right: 'À la suite de' is the standard prepositional locution.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'quant' requires 'à': 'quant au'.
optionCases.b: Right: 'quant au calendrier' is correct.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'en ce qui a trait' requires 'à': 'en ce qui a trait au'.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'en ce qui concerne' takes a direct complement, without 'de'.

optionCases.a: Right: 'différent' governs 'de': 'différent de celui'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 's'adressaient' correctly agrees with 'publications' (plural).
optionCases.c: Wrong: 's'adresser à' is correct; 'pour' would be wrong.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'adopté dans cette campagne' is correct.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'au plus tard au 15 mars' is not standard; the date takes 'le'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'avant ou le' is a calque of 'on or before'.
optionCases.c: Right: 'au plus tard le 15 mars' is the standard construction.
optionCases.d: Wrong in register: 'pas plus tard que' is a calque of 'no later than'.

optionCases.a: Wrong in register: 'dépendamment de' is a criticized regionalism not used in formal writing.
optionCases.b: Wrong: the locution is 'en fonction de', not 'en fonction à'.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'en relation des' is not a French construction.
optionCases.d: Right: 'en fonction des ressources' is the standard construction.

optionCases.a: Wrong in nuance: 'en rapport avec' means 'related to', not 'compared with'.
optionCases.b: Right: 'par rapport à' expresses a comparison with the previous year.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'rapport à' without 'par' is familiar and incorrect in this register.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'en rapport à' is not standard.

optionCases.a: Wrong in register: 'vis-à-vis' requires 'de' in careful writing ('vis-à-vis des').
optionCases.b: Wrong: the locution is 'à l'égard de', not 'à l'égard à'.
optionCases.c: Right: 'à l'égard des employés' is the standard construction.
optionCases.d: Wrong in register: figurative 'au niveau de' is criticized.

optionCases.a: Right: 'dans les dix jours ouvrables suivant' expresses a deadline window.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'en dix jours ouvrables suivant' is not idiomatic.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'dans dix jours' means 'ten days from now', and does not combine with 'suivant'.
optionCases.d: Wrong in register: 'en dedans de' is a familiar Quebec usage.

optionCases.a: Wrong: in 'se dire fière', 'se' is the direct object, so 'dite' agrees with the feminine subject.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'conformes' correctly agrees with 'documents' (plural).
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'conforme aux normes' is correct.
optionCases.d: Right: 'fier' governs 'de': 'fière du travail'.

optionCases.a: Wrong: 'remédier' requires 'à' before its complement.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'remédier sur' is not a French construction.
optionCases.c: Right: 'remédier à la hausse' is the correct construction.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'pallier' is transitive direct; 'pallier à' is criticized.

optionCases.a: Wrong in register: 'se fier sur' is a regional usage that is not accepted in careful writing.
optionCases.b: Right: 'se fier au calculateur' is the standard construction.
optionCases.c: Wrong: 'se confier à' means to confide in someone.
optionCases.d: Wrong: 'se fier de' is not a French construction.

optionCases.a: Right: 'pallier' is transitive direct: 'pallier le manque'.
optionCases.b: Wrong: 'procéder à l'installation' is correct.
optionCases.c: Wrong: this keeps the incorrect 'pallier à' and needlessly pluralizes 'manque'.
